name: Sphinx rump passage and cavities
note: Mapped by the ARCE Sphinx Project; small, dead-end, documented.

name: Osiris Shaft
note: Three levels to about 30 m below the Khafre causeway, water at the bottom. Real, excavated, and the model's first genuinely subterranean structure.

name: Subterranean chamber of the Great Pyramid
ScanPyramids Big Void
note: Muon tomography, peer reviewed; position with error bars, inclination open.

name: ScanPyramids north-face corridor
note: Muon tomography confirmed by endoscope in 2023.

name: Cavity beneath the Sphinx's forepaws
note: Seismic refraction anomaly interpreted as a possible chamber about 5 m down; never excavated.

name: Khafre Project SAR shafts and complex
note: Five 'Zed' structures in the pyramid's base; eight vertical wells in two north–south rows, wrapped in descending spirals, falling 648 m below the base into two cubes about 80 m a side; structures about 2 km down. From the team's conference abstract of 16 March 2025 (SAR Doppler tomography of Capella and Umbra data); its figures are in g2-sar.json. Not peer reviewed, and the method's only peer-reviewed paper (on Khufu, 2022) was retracted on 10 August 2026. Radar specialists dispute that surface vibrations seen from orbit can be inverted to these depths. Hawass, a former minister, called it false, and the Ministry authorized no work at Khafre. Modelled as a claim, rendered as such.

name: Hall of Records
note: Edgar Cayce's readings placed a chamber of Atlantean records under the Sphinx's paw. No physical evidence; registered so the viewer can show what the claim asserts.

name: Obelisk of Senusret I, Heliopolis
note: About 24 km north-east of Giza, which is 16.7 km east and 16.7 km north, in the same WGS84 datum and the Giza frame; the target of claim D1.

name: Sphinx Temple
note: The temple directly in front of the Sphinx's paws, surveyed by Nell and Ruggles in 2006; its measurement keys carry the prefix sphinx_temple, a key having no hyphens in it.

name: Valley temple of Khafre
note: The temple beside the Sphinx Temple, sharing the passage between the two; its measurement keys carry the prefix khafre_valley_temple.

name: Causeway of Khafre
note: The 495 m causeway running west-north-west from the valley temple up to Khafre's pyramid; its measurement keys carry the prefix khafre_causeway.

name: Head of the Delta, the barrage at El-Qanater el-Khayreya
note: A place rather than a monument: the point about 23 km north of Giza where the Nile divides, registered so claim D3 has something to take a bearing to.

name: Western corner of the Delta, Alexandria
note: A place rather than a monument, and a modern town standing for the Canopic mouth at the Delta's western limit.

name: Eastern corner of the Delta, Port Said
note: A place rather than a monument, and a modern town standing for the Pelusiac mouth at the Delta's eastern limit.

name: The plateau's lesser monuments (Tier 3)
note: The queens' and satellite pyramids, Khentkawes, the four temples of Khafre and Menkaure, the Sphinx Temple and Amenhotep II's, the boat pits east of Khufu, the Wall of the Crow and the mastaba fields, as massing solids from OSM footprints registered onto the survey. Every one is excavated; what is not measured is their height, which is a seked-estimate where OSM gives none.

name: Pyramid of Amenemhat III at Hawara
note: Mud brick, once cased in limestone; entered by Petrie in 1889, its burial chamber a single quartzite block. The Labyrinth's remains lie to its south.

name: The Labyrinth's foundation platform
note: Amenemhat III's mortuary temple, quarried away in antiquity to its beds of limestone chips and beton, which Petrie traced to about 1000 by 800 ft south of the pyramid. Herodotus's and Strabo's Labyrinth; Petrie's restored plan of courts and a columned hall (1912) is an interpretation.

name: VLF-EM anomalies south of the pyramid (the 2008 survey, as published)
note: The 2008 NRIAG survey's peer-reviewed result: elongated and square conductive anomalies at shallow depth on a 2 m grid, which the authors compare with Herodotus. Instrumented because it is published in a refereed journal (night decision 27); the deeper walls its organiser reports are hawara.mataha-walls.

name: Resistivity closures south of the pyramid
note: High-resistivity closures in inverted ERT sections, 6 m wide at about 7.5 m and 4 m wide at 5 m, which the authors say may be archaeological remains needing excavation. The 2008 survey's leader is among the authors.

name: Walls reported 8–12 m down (Mataha Expedition, 2008)
note: Thick walls and nearly closed rooms 8–12 m down over hectares, and a wall over 17 m deep, as the expedition's organiser reports them. The NRIAG report is unpublished, so the tier is claimed (night decision 27).

name: Merlin Burrows multi-level complex
note: Four or five levels 20–50 m apart, to about 100 m, and two chambers under the pyramid, from satellite scans of 2015 by an undisclosed method. Depths no radar reaches.

name: Carlotto's areas of uncorrelated radar return
note: Two areas either side of the canal south of the pyramid, outlined from Sentinel-1 and ALOS PALSAR. By the author's own figures the radar reaches 0.5–5 m. Claimed, not instrumented: the outlines are his reading of unexplained returns, not a located structure (night decision 33; plan decision 11 asks Stewart).

name: The Labyrinth's underground half
note: Herodotus's 1,500 underground rooms, the tombs of the builders and of sacred crocodiles, which he was not shown and reports from hearsay. Nobody since has seen them.

name: The plateau's water table
note: Mapped by ERT, seismic refraction, GPR and boreholes, peer reviewed. Not a monument: it is here because chapter 8's reply draws it in the section, where any shaft hundreds of metres deep would stand far below it.
